Evidence-scope guard: the head-and-neck squamous-cell-carcinoma risk literature belongs to recessive dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa, a hereditary mechanobullous disease with a different biology from acquired EBA; the SCC pathway is recorded as an out-of-scope negative screen rather than an edge (identity-scope guard under the alopecia/areata precedent).
governanceNotes: D1 batch 29 (2026-09-23): one bounded esophageal-stricture association authored from the EBA esophageal-involvement literature (Figueredo 2021 and Moura 2011 case reports of EBA-provoked esophageal stricture requiring endoscopic dilation, anchored in the Lambert 2026 subepidermal-blistering-disease review of antibody-class-driven mucosal scarring); the case-class guard and the mucosal-involvement rarity of EBA relative to pemphigoid are recorded.

No squamous-cell-carcinoma, corneal-scarring, or contractures edge was authored: the SCC-in-EB literature is recessive-dystrophic-EB scoped, EBA corneal and digital outcomes lack quantitative association studies beyond case reports, and the scar-target edges would overlap the identity's own blister-scarring presentation (manifestation guard); all three pathways are recorded here.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Esophageal involvement with stricture formation is documented in epidermolysis bullosa acquisita: Figueredo 2021 reports an EBA patient with esophageal stricture requiring serial endoscopic intervention, Moura 2011 reports EBA complicated by esophageal stenosis managed endoscopically, and the Lambert 2026 review of subepidermal autoimmune blistering disease links antibody class and target antigen to mucosal scarring phenotypes; blister-scar cycles in the esophageal mucosa are the accepted mechanism in the case-class literature.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established at the mapping level: the evidence is case-report class without denominators (EBA esophageal involvement is rare), strictures in esophageal disease require exclusion of caustic injury, medication esophagitis, reflux disease, radiation, and malignancy, and mucosal involvement in EBA is uncommon relative to skin-predominant presentations; the mapping asserts the documented association, not a population rate.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: A hypothesized blister-scar stenosis pathway: antibodies to type VII collagen anchor the subepidermal blister plane, and repeated mucosal blistering, erosion, and healing across the esophageal circumference lays down fibrotic scar that contracts the lumen into a fixed stricture, producing progressive dysphagia and food impaction; endoscopic dilation provides temporary relief while the immunologic blistering continues. Individual attribution requires biopsy-proven EBA with direct immunofluorescence and endoscopic visualization.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: The association rests on case reports and review-class mechanistic reasoning without cohort denominators; competing stricture etiologies are common in the same age range and must be excluded endoscopically and histologically, mucosal EBA involvement must be biopsy-proven with linear IgG deposition along the basement membrane, and no probability estimate is asserted.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Biopsy-proven EBA by histology and direct immunofluorescence (subepidermal blister with type VII collagen antibodies); endoscopically documented stricture with chronology compatible with blistering activity; exclusion of caustic, radiation, medication-induced, reflux, and malignant strictures; gastroenterology and dermatology assessment of the individual relationship
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Prior radiation to the mediastinum or esophagus
Eosinophilic esophagitis or other inflammatory stenosis

suggestions.rationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY: the blister-scar stenosis mechanism is biologically specific and case-documented, but the evidence base is case-report class in a rare manifestation and competing etiologies are common; no causation is forced.
